# What this notebook does

Kate, 2026-11-18. One heatmap of **fit-weighted SHAP** from the intrinsic-feature regression forest,
fitted separately to the **cells' own hypoxic TE response**: siCTRL TE log2(hypoxia / normoxia), no
knockdown. Positive outcome = TE higher in hypoxia.

- **Columns:** MDA-MB-231 at 1, 4 and 24hr (`10y_sictrl_hypoxia_outcome_prep.R`, spike-in
  normalized) and MCF7-SIX1 at 1hr (`10ym_mcf7six1_sictrl_hypoxia_outcome_prep.R`, `lfcShrink`-shrunk,
  not spike-in normalized; MCF7-SIX1 has no later timepoint).
- **Rows:** every intrinsic feature, grouped by feature family.
- **Cell value = share x held-out Spearman^2, signed.** The share is the feature's fraction of the
  model's total mean |SHAP| (unitless, so the log2 fold-change scale of the contrast drops out).
  Multiplying by the model's held-out Spearman^2 makes each **column sum to its own held-out
  Spearman^2**, so brightness shows how well that model ordered genes it never trained on. A cell
  reads roughly as "the part of the explained rank variation this feature carries" (Spearman^2 is
  R^2 on ranks, not variance explained on the log2 scale). The sign is the feature's direction
  (`shap_value_cor`, the correlation of a feature's value with its own SHAP value: + means higher
  values of the feature push the prediction toward higher TE in hypoxia). SHAP is averaged over each
  model's **200 held-out genes** (the explain set of `11_shap_regression.Rmd`), never training genes.
- **Why not raw SHAP.** Raw SHAP is in log2 TE units, so a contrast with widely spread fold changes
  looks brighter whether or not its model is better. **Why not SHAP / outcome sd.** That removes the
  scale, but brightness would then track how widely the predictions spread, and a model can spread
  its predictions confidently and still be wrong. Held-out fit measures being right.
- **Why Spearman^2, not R^2** (decided with Kate 2026-11-18). These TE fold changes are
  heavy-tailed: in MCF7-SIX1 1% of held-out genes hold 59% of the outcome variance (kurtosis ~180),
  and both cell lines' values are `lfcShrink(type = "apeglm")`-shrunk (`code/functions.R`
  `deFunction`; MCF7-SIX1's `5_hypoxicresponse.Rmd`), so a fold change's size partly reflects read
  depth. R^2 (squared Pearson) is set by those few extreme genes; dropping just the top 1% brings
  R^2 to almost exactly Spearman^2 in every column (section 3 checks this). The question here is
  which features **order** genes by TE response, which ranks answer directly.
- **Held-out** = the 20% of genes the forest never trained on (`spearman_raw_y` from
  `10_rf_regression.Rmd`).

**The trade-off.** On one shared color scale a weak model (Spearman^2 ~0.14) is pale everywhere, so its
feature pattern is harder to see. The shares on their own (unweighted) are in the exported values
table for reading the pattern within a weak column.

**Direction stability is not measured for these models.** Whether a feature's sign repeats across
train/test splits has only been swept for si3d hypoxia 1hr and does not transfer, so no cell is
marked. Run `11d_shap_regression_seed_sweep.R` on these four models before reading the direction of
a small cell.

Each column is on its own cell line's genes and dominant transcripts (MDA-MB-231 10,172 genes,
MCF7-SIX1 its own isoform matrix), so they are separate models, not one model scored twice.

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(here); library(pheatmap); library(grid) })
source(here("code", "translational_control_overview", "feature_colours.R"))
O <- here("output", "translational_control_overview")
SAVE <- isTRUE(params$save_plots)
TOL <- 1e-9
```

# 1. Load the four runs

```{r load}
ex <- strsplit(strsplit(params$experiments, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], "=", fixed = TRUE)
exps <- tibble(label = map_chr(ex, 1), suffix = map_chr(ex, 2))
stopifnot("duplicate column labels" = !anyDuplicated(exps$label))
f <- function(stem, s) file.path(O, paste0(stem, "_", s, ".csv"))
miss <- unlist(lapply(exps$suffix, function(s) {
  p <- c(f("shapreg_per_gene", s), f("shapreg_feature", s), f("rfreg_performance", s), f("shapreg_qc", s))
  p[!file.exists(p)] }))
stopifnot("missing run outputs - knit 10_ and 11_ for every column first" = !length(miss))

ann <- read_csv(file.path(O, "feature_annotation.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
per_gene <- setNames(lapply(exps$suffix, function(s) read_csv(f("shapreg_per_gene", s), show_col_types = FALSE)), exps$label)
feat     <- setNames(lapply(exps$suffix, function(s) read_csv(f("shapreg_feature", s), show_col_types = FALSE)), exps$label)
perf     <- setNames(lapply(exps$suffix, function(s) read_csv(f("rfreg_performance", s), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
                                deframe()), exps$label)
qc       <- setNames(lapply(exps$suffix, function(s) read_csv(f("shapreg_qc", s), show_col_types = FALSE)), exps$label)
```

# 2. Checks

```{r checks}
features <- feat[[1]]$feature
for (lab in exps$label) {
  pg <- per_gene[[lab]]; ft <- feat[[lab]]; q <- qc[[lab]]
  fc <- setdiff(colnames(pg), c("gene_id_clean", "symbol", "y", "pred"))
  # The same intrinsic feature set in every column, or the rows would mean different things.
  stopifnot("feature set differs between columns" = setequal(fc, features) && setequal(ft$feature, features),
            "every row must be an intrinsic feature" = all(ann$block[match(features, ann$feature)] == "intrinsic"),
            "per-gene SHAP is not the 200-gene held-out explain set" = nrow(pg) == q$explain_n,
            "duplicate genes in the explain set" = !anyDuplicated(pg$gene_id_clean),
            "outcome is raw log2 TE, not transformed" = q$target_transform == "raw")
  # Recompute mean |SHAP| from the per-gene values; it must reproduce 11_'s saved summary.
  m <- colMeans(abs(as.matrix(pg[, ft$feature])))
  stopifnot("per-gene SHAP does not reproduce mean_abs_shap" = max(abs(m - ft$mean_abs_shap)) < TOL)
  # SHAP is additive: baseline + sum over features = the forest's prediction, for every gene.
  clos <- pg$pred - rowSums(as.matrix(pg[, fc])) - q$baseline
  stopifnot("SHAP does not sum to the prediction" = max(abs(clos)) < 1e-6)
  # The model must beat its own permuted-outcome refit, or its SHAP describes noise.
  stopifnot("model does not beat its permuted-outcome null" = perf[[lab]][["spearman_raw_y"]] > perf[[lab]][["perm_spearman"]])
}
cat(sprintf("%d columns x %d intrinsic features; all checks passed\n", nrow(exps), length(features)))
```

# 3. Fit and outcome spread

Held-out = the 20% of genes the forest never trained on. `perm` is the same model refit on a
permuted outcome, i.e. what a model with no real signal scores.

```{r fit_table}
fit <- exps %>% mutate(
  n_genes   = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["n_genes"]]),
  n_test    = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["n_test"]]),
  heldout_R2       = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["r2_pearson_sq_raw_y"]]),
  heldout_spearman = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["spearman_raw_y"]]),
  perm_spearman    = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["perm_spearman"]]),
  outcome_sd       = map_dbl(label, ~ perf[[.x]][["target_sd"]]),
  # Kept in the exported CSV only, not shown: it tracks the outcome's spread more than the fit
  # (24hr is 2.3x 1hr while predicting worse), so displaying it invites the wrong reading.
  total_abs_shap   = map_dbl(label, ~ sum(feat[[.x]]$mean_abs_shap)),
  heldout_spearman2 = heldout_spearman^2)
stopifnot("a model ranks held-out genes backwards - squaring would hide it" = all(fit$heldout_spearman > 0))
knitr::kable(fit %>% dplyr::select(-suffix, -total_abs_shap), digits = 3)
```

## Why the weight is Spearman^2: the outcome's tails

Recomputed from the saved held-out predictions. If R^2 is set by a few extreme genes, removing the
1% furthest from the mean should move R^2 most of the way to Spearman^2.

```{r tails}
tails <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(exps)), function(i) {
  p <- read_csv(f("rfreg_predictions", exps$suffix[i]), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(split == "test")
  stopifnot("held-out predictions do not match the saved n_test" = nrow(p) == fit$n_test[i],
            "held-out predictions do not reproduce the saved Spearman" =
              abs(cor(p$y, p$pred, method = "spearman") - fit$heldout_spearman[i]) < 1e-9)
  ss <- (p$y - mean(p$y))^2; top <- order(-ss)[seq_len(round(0.01 * nrow(p)))]
  tibble(label = exps$label[i], n_test = nrow(p),
         R2 = cor(p$y, p$pred)^2, R2_drop_top1pct = cor(p$y[-top], p$pred[-top])^2,
         spearman2 = cor(p$y, p$pred, method = "spearman")^2,
         pct_variance_in_top1pct = 100 * sum(ss[top]) / sum(ss),
         kurtosis = mean(((p$y - mean(p$y)) / sd(p$y))^4))
})
knitr::kable(tails, digits = 3)
```

```{r fit_plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.2}
pf <- fit %>% dplyr::select(label, n_test, `held-out R^2` = heldout_R2, `held-out Spearman` = heldout_spearman) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(label, n_test)) %>% mutate(label = factor(label, exps$label))
gfit <- ggplot(pf, aes(label, value)) + geom_col(fill = "grey40", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", value)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "How well each model predicts held-out genes",
       subtitle = sprintf("siCTRL TE log2(hypoxia / normoxia); n held-out = %s",
                          paste(sprintf("%s %d", fit$label, fit$n_test), collapse = ", "))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
gfit
if (SAVE) ggsave(here("plots", "50_raw_shap_hypvsnor_fit.pdf"), gfit, width = 7, height = 3.2)
```

# 4. Raw SHAP heatmap

```{r matrix}
# share = mean |SHAP| / sum over features (recomputed, then checked against 11_'s share_pct);
# cell = share x held-out Spearman^2 x sign(shap_value_cor), so |cells| in a column sum to its
# Spearman^2. (`r2` holds Spearman^2; the name is kept so the code below reads unchanged.)
r2 <- setNames(fit$heldout_spearman2, fit$label)
share <- sapply(exps$label, function(lab) {
  ft <- feat[[lab]]; s <- ft$mean_abs_shap / sum(ft$mean_abs_shap)
  stopifnot("recomputed share does not reproduce 11_'s share_pct" = max(abs(100 * s - ft$share_pct)) < 1e-6)
  setNames(s, ft$feature)[features] })
sgn <- sapply(exps$label, function(lab) { ft <- feat[[lab]]; setNames(sign(ft$shap_value_cor), ft$feature)[features] })
stopifnot("NA share" = !anyNA(share))
# A direction is undefined when shap_value_cor is NA - a feature constant across the 200 explained
# genes (e.g. a binary flag). Its magnitude is real but it has no sign, so the cell is drawn grey
# rather than given an arbitrary sign or dropped. Asserted to be negligible, so grey never hides a
# feature that matters.
nodir <- which(is.na(sgn), arr.ind = TRUE)
if (nrow(nodir)) {
  nd <- tibble(feature = rownames(sgn)[nodir[, 1]], experiment = colnames(sgn)[nodir[, 2]],
               share_pct = 100 * share[nodir])
  print(nd)
  stopifnot("a feature with no direction carries a non-negligible share" = all(nd$share_pct < 1))
}
weighted <- sweep(share, 2, r2[colnames(share)], `*`)
stopifnot("a column's weighted shares do not sum to its held-out Spearman^2" =
            max(abs(colSums(weighted) - r2[colnames(weighted)])) < 1e-9)
cellv <- weighted * sgn

fam <- ann$family[match(features, ann$feature)]
reg <- feature_category(features, ann)
# Families ordered by their total |cell| over all columns; features by |cell| within a family.
fam_order <- names(sort(tapply(rowSums(weighted), fam, sum), decreasing = TRUE))
o <- order(match(fam, fam_order), -rowSums(weighted))
M <- cellv[o, , drop = FALSE]; fam_o <- fam[o]
rownames(M) <- paste(fam_o, "|", rownames(M))
gaps <- which(head(fam_o, -1) != tail(fam_o, -1))

annor <- data.frame(region = reg[o], row.names = rownames(M))
# The outcome sd is not shown: the cells are shares x Spearman^2, neither of which depends on the
# outcome's spread, and on these heavy-tailed fold changes the sd is set by a few extreme genes.
# R^2 is not shown either: the brightness is Spearman^2, and R^2 beside it invites the comparison
# the tails section already settles. It stays in the fit table and the tails table.
annoc <- data.frame(`held-out Spearman2` = fit$heldout_spearman2,
                    check.names = FALSE, row.names = exps$label)
lim <- max(abs(M), na.rm = TRUE)
brks <- seq(-lim, lim, length.out = 101)
ac <- list(region = FEATURE_COLOURS[levels(droplevels(reg))],
           `held-out Spearman2` = c("white", "grey20"))
# Wrap "MDA-MB-231 1hr" onto two lines at the last space, so horizontal labels fit their column.
lab_col <- sub(" (\\S+)$", "\n\\1", exps$label)

draw_hm <- function() pheatmap(M, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, gaps_row = gaps,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(100), breaks = brks,
  annotation_row = annor, annotation_col = annoc, annotation_colors = ac, labels_col = lab_col,
  angle_col = 0, fontsize_row = 7, fontsize_col = 8, cellwidth = 70, cellheight = 9, border_color = NA,
  display_numbers = matrix(ifelse(is.na(M), "no dir", sprintf("%.3f", M)), nrow(M)), na_col = "grey85",
  number_color = "grey20", fontsize_number = 5.5,
  annotation_names_row = FALSE,
  main = sprintf("siCTRL TE log2(hypoxia / normoxia)\nSHAP share x held-out Spearman2, signed by direction\neach column sums to its Spearman2\nn = 200 held-out genes per column, %d intrinsic features\ndirection stability not measured",
                 nrow(M)), fontsize = 9, silent = TRUE)
ph <- draw_hm()

# Print each fit value inside its own annotation box. pheatmap draws the column annotation as one
# rectGrob whose rectangles run over expand.grid(column, annotation track) - the same column-major
# order as as.matrix(annoc[colnames(M), ]) - so the labels are built in that order and placed on the
# rectangles' own coordinates. Asserted below by matching every fill colour to the value it encodes.
add_box_labels <- function(gt) {
  i <- which(gt$layout$name == "col_annotation")
  stopifnot("no column annotation grob found" = length(i) == 1)
  rg <- gt$grobs[[i]]
  vals <- as.matrix(annoc[colnames(M), , drop = FALSE])
  stopifnot("annotation box count does not match columns x tracks" = length(rg$gp$fill) == length(vals))
  # Each fill must be the colour pheatmap's ramp gives that value, or the labels are misplaced.
  ramp_col <- function(v, x) colorRampPalette(c("white", "grey20"))(100)[
    as.numeric(cut(x, breaks = seq(min(v), max(v), length.out = 101), include.lowest = TRUE))]
  expect <- as.vector(sapply(seq_len(ncol(vals)), function(j) ramp_col(vals[, j], vals[, j])))
  stopifnot("annotation labels would not line up with their boxes" = all(toupper(rg$gp$fill) == toupper(expect)))
  dark <- colSums(col2rgb(rg$gp$fill)) < 3 * 128
  tg <- textGrob(sprintf("%.2f", as.vector(vals)), x = rg$x, y = rg$y,
                 gp = gpar(fontsize = 7, col = ifelse(dark, "white", "black")))
  gt$grobs[[i]] <- grobTree(rg, tg)
  gt
}
ph$gtable <- add_box_labels(ph$gtable)
```

```{r heatmap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 10}
grid.newpage(); grid.draw(ph$gtable)
if (SAVE) { pdf(here("plots", "50_raw_shap_heatmap_hypvsnor.pdf"), width = 11, height = 10)
            grid.newpage(); grid.draw(ph$gtable); dev.off() }
```

Blue = higher values of the feature push the prediction toward **lower** TE in hypoxia; vermillion =
toward **higher** TE in hypoxia. Color limits are symmetric and shared by all four columns
(+/- `r signif(lim, 3)`, in units of held-out Spearman^2), so a pale column is a model that
ordered held-out genes poorly, not a contrast with small fold changes.

# 5. Values

```{r export}
# Long format: the plotted value plus the unweighted share and direction it was built from.
out <- tibble(feature = rep(features, ncol(cellv)), experiment = rep(colnames(cellv), each = length(features)),
              family = rep(fam, ncol(cellv)), region = rep(as.character(reg), ncol(cellv)),
              share = as.vector(share), direction = as.vector(sgn),
              heldout_spearman2 = rep(r2[colnames(cellv)], each = length(features)),
              share_x_spearman2_signed = as.vector(cellv))
write_csv(out, file.path(O, "raw_shap_heatmap_hypvsnor_values.csv"))
write_csv(fit, file.path(O, "raw_shap_heatmap_hypvsnor_fit.csv"))
knitr::kable(as_tibble(M, rownames = "family | feature") %>% slice_head(n = 15), digits = 4,
             caption = "Top 15 rows as plotted")
```
